claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I need to gather some information about your situation. Let me start with the basics.

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm interested in finding out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - his name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child named Alex.

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thanks for letting me know Alex is 17 years old.

Since Alex is 16 or over, the rules are a bit different. **Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** For example, is he at school, college, university, or doing an apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's not in school or college anymore, but he has just started an apprenticeship.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I need to check on an important detail about Alex's apprenticeship.

**Is Alex's apprenticeship in England?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it is - he's doing his apprenticeship in England.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate you providing that information. Unfortunately, I need to let you know about an important rule regarding Child Benefit.

According to the eligibility rules, **you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts an apprenticeship in England**. Since Alex has just started an apprenticeship in England, he would no longer be eligible for Child Benefit.

Let me confirm I have all the details correct before I provide my final assessment:
- You have one child named Alex
- Alex is 17 years old
- Alex has just started an apprenticeship in England

Is that all correct, or is there anything else about Alex's situation I should know about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's all correct. Alex lives with me here in England, and he's just started his apprenticeship.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming those details. I now have all the information I need to provide you with my final assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Summary

I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Why:** Although you would normally qualify for Child Benefit for a child under 20 who is in approved education or training, there is a specific rule that ends eligibility when a child starts an apprenticeship in England. Since Alex has just started his apprenticeship in England, he no longer qualifies for Child Benefit.

If you have any questions about this decision or if Alex's circumstances change in the future, you can contact HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) for further advice.
